issues.description: Substring match on '--version' output will mis-identify any tool whose name contains 'conda'/'mamba'
issues.detail: validate_conda accepts anything whose --version output contains 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' as a substring. 'mamba' is contained in 'micromamba', which is fine, but the check is sloppy: any random binary that prints those substrings passes. Match on the leading token of the version string, or check the basename.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the file picker breaks Linux and macOS users
issues.detail: On Linux/macOS the conda/mamba/micromamba binaries do not have a .exe extension. Hardcoding '*.exe' as the file dialog filter means users on every non-Windows platform get an empty file picker by default. Either platform-gate the filter or drop it.

issues.description: Empty string is reported as a valid conda executable
issues.detail: validate_conda returns True for ''. That is a lie dressed up as convenience for the empty-textbox case. The UI layer should decide that empty means 'unset'; the validator should say False for 'not a conda executable'. Otherwise downstream code can't trust the function name.

issues.description: run_program subprocess is never waited on or closed; leaks file descriptors on every validation
issues.detail: run_program(...).communicate() captures stdout but the Popen object is discarded without checking returncode or closing pipes explicitly. Over a session of typing in a path field with live validation this leaks. Bind it to a variable, check returncode, and let it close cleanly.

issues.description: Indentation inside the generator expression does not match the surrounding codebase style
issues.detail: The 'for tool in [...]' line is indented one extra level inside an any(...) generator. The rest of the file is PEP8-conventional. Match the existing voice; don't invent a new one for four lines.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to a generic helper changes behavior for every other browsefile caller
issues.detail: create_browsefile is shared infrastructure. Adding edit.setFocus() after select_file changes focus behavior for every preference page in Spyder that uses it, not just this one. If you need focus for the conda case, do it in the caller, not in the shared widget code.

review.summary: Patch does one thing — adds a user-configurable conda executable — and the diff is reasonably scoped. The shape is right, but it ships sloppy validation: substring matching that's too loose, a Windows-only file filter that breaks Linux/macOS users, a validator that lies about empty strings, and a leaked subprocess on every keystroke. The shared widget helper also grew a setFocus side effect that affects every other caller, which is the kind of change that bites maintainers later. NEEDS-WORK — fix the validator, fix the filter, move the focus call to the caller, then land it.
